titulo: Can it be too cold to snow?
fuentes: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Severe Weather 101 - Winter Weather FAQ: https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/winter/faq/ ('It rarely snows when the temperature drops below zero degrees Fahrenheit' because 'the atmosphere is too stable'; 'it is too cold to snow' really means 'there is not enough lifting of air to cause snow to reach the surface'; 'Even at very cold surface temperatures, significant snowfall can occur.')
destinatario: se lo manda alguien a su amigo que dice 'hace demasiado frío para que nieve' para corregirlo
receta: el que lo hace mal (mito del frío) con capa de datos

frases.texto: You've said it yourself: it's too cold to snow.
frases.estilo: Dry and confident, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The National Severe Storms Laboratory says it rarely snows below zero degrees Fahrenheit.
But not because it's too cold. It's because the air is too stable.
frases.estilo: Explaining simply, like to a friend.

frases.texto: Snow needs air lifting upward. Without enough lift, it never reaches the ground.
So when people say it's too cold to snow, what they really mean is not enough lift.
NOAA says even at very cold surface temperatures, significant snowfall can occur.
Heads up: below zero, snow really is rare. It's just not a temperature limit.
So next time it's bitter cold and cloudy, don't write off the snow.
Send this to the friend who says it's too cold to snow.
frases.estilo: Playful, with humor, as a punchline.
